# Richness Projection

This page derives the projection contribution to the observed cluster richness
distribution implemented by [[numcosmo|NcClusterRichnessProjection]].

## The Contaminated Likelihood

The observed richness $\lambda$ of a cluster of mass $M$ at redshift $z$ is
modelled as a two-component mixture: a clean fraction $1-f_\mathrm{proj}$ that
follows the log-normal mass--richness relation, and a projected fraction
$f_\mathrm{proj}$ whose richness is inflated by unassociated structure along the
line of sight,
$$
P(\lambda \mid M, z) = (1-f_\mathrm{proj}) \, f_\mathrm{LN}(\lambda \mid \mu, \sigma)
                     + f_\mathrm{proj} \, T(\lambda),
$$
with $\mu(M, z)$ and $\sigma(M, z)$ the location and scale of the log-normal.
The projected term is usually written
$$
T(\lambda) = \frac{\tau}{\sqrt{\pi}} e^{-\tau\lambda}
             \int_{-\infty}^{L} e^{-y^2 + \tau e^{\mu + \sqrt{2}\sigma y}} \, \mathrm{d}y,
\qquad
L = \frac{\ln\lambda - \mu}{\sqrt{2}\sigma}.
$$

In this form the integrand reaches $e^{-L^2 + \tau\lambda}$ at the upper limit
and is brought back down only by the prefactor $e^{-\tau\lambda}$. For
$\tau\lambda \sim 300$ that intermediate value is $e^{300}$, so a quadrature has
to carry a number near the top of the double range to return one near the
bottom.

## Change of Variables

Substituting $t = e^{\mu + \sqrt{2}\sigma y}$ removes the difficulty. The new
variable is the true richness: $y$ is the standardized $\ln\lambda_\mathrm{true}$,
so
$$
y = \frac{\ln t - \mu}{\sqrt{2}\sigma},
\qquad
\mathrm{d}y = \frac{\mathrm{d}t}{\sqrt{2}\,\sigma\,t}.
$$
The limits become physical, $y \to -\infty \Rightarrow t \to 0^+$ and
$y = L \Rightarrow t = \lambda$, the $\sqrt{2}\sigma$ cancelling exactly. Both
exponentials simplify,
$$
e^{-y^2} = \exp\left[-\frac{(\ln t - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right],
\qquad
e^{+\tau e^{\mu + \sqrt{2}\sigma y}} = e^{\tau t},
$$
and, since $\sqrt{\pi}\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{2\pi}$, the surviving measure is the
log-normal density itself,
$$
\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\,\sigma t}
\exp\left[-\frac{(\ln t - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right]
= f_\mathrm{LN}(t \mid \mu, \sigma).
$$
Pairing the prefactor with the integrand, $e^{-\tau\lambda} e^{\tau t} =
e^{-\tau(\lambda - t)} \le 1$ for $t \le \lambda$, leaves
$$
T(\lambda) = \tau \int_0^{\lambda} f_\mathrm{LN}(t \mid \mu, \sigma)
             \, e^{-\tau(\lambda - t)} \, \mathrm{d}t .
$$

## Interpretation

The result is the density of a sum of independent variables,
$$
\lambda = \lambda_\mathrm{true} + \Delta,
\qquad
\lambda_\mathrm{true} \sim \mathrm{LogNormal}(\mu, \sigma),
\qquad
\Delta \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\tau) .
$$
Projection adds member galaxies, by an exponentially distributed amount of mean
$1/\tau$. Two consequences follow. First, $T$ is normalized on its own, so the
mixture above needs no correction factor. Second, $T \to f_\mathrm{LN}$ as
$\tau \to \infty$, when nothing is added.

## The ODE

Differentiating under the integral sign, the boundary term contributes
$\tau f_\mathrm{LN}(\lambda)$ and the $\lambda$ in the exponential reproduces
$-\tau T$:
$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}T}{\mathrm{d}\lambda} = \tau \left[ f_\mathrm{LN}(\lambda) - T(\lambda) \right],
\qquad
T(0) = 0 .
$$
This is a first-order linear ODE with bounded coefficients, integrated by
[[numcosmo-math|NcmOdeSpline]]. A single solve covers every $\lambda$ at fixed
$(\ln M, z)$, whereas a quadrature of the original expression runs once per
point.

The class integrates in $x = \ln\lambda$, where $\lambda f_\mathrm{LN}(\lambda)$
is the log-normal density in $\ln\lambda$ and $\lambda$ drops out of the source
term,
$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}T}{\mathrm{d}x}
= \tau \left[ \frac{1}{\sigma} \varphi\!\left(\frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}\right) - e^{x} T \right],
\qquad
\varphi(u) = \frac{e^{-u^2/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}} .
$$
Integration starts at $x_i = \mu - 10\sigma$, and the density is reported as zero
below that point.

The initial value there is not zero. $T(x_i)$ is bounded by $\tau
F_\mathrm{LN}(x_i)$ and by $f_\mathrm{LN}(x_i)$, each attained in one of the two
limits of $\tau$, so the smaller of the two is correct to the $10^{-23}$ scale of
both. Starting from $T = 0$ instead leaves the solver with no scale for its error
test, and any absolute tolerance small enough for the tail is then rejected on
the first step.

The depth $10\sigma$ follows from the error of that initial value rather than
from conditioning: it enters the solution as a fraction $\Phi(-n)$ of the peak,
measured at $3.3 \times 10^{-5}$ for $n = 4$ and below $10^{-8}$ for $n \ge 8$.
A minimum knot density is imposed on the solver output as well, since $T$ is
$f_\mathrm{LN}$ smoothed by a kernel of width $1/\tau$ and so never varies faster
than $\sigma$ in $x$.

## Cumulative Distribution

Integrating the ODE from $0$ to $\lambda$ and rearranging gives the cumulative
in closed form in terms of the solution already available,
$$
\int_0^{\lambda} T(\lambda') \, \mathrm{d}\lambda'
= F_\mathrm{LN}(\lambda) - \frac{T(\lambda)}{\tau},
\qquad
F_\mathrm{LN}(\lambda) = \frac{1}{2}
  \mathrm{erfc}\!\left(\frac{\mu - \ln\lambda}{\sqrt{2}\sigma}\right),
$$
so a bin integral costs two spline evaluations and two $\mathrm{erfc}$ calls,
with no second ODE and no quadrature. Taking $\lambda \to \infty$, where
$T \to 0$ and $F_\mathrm{LN} \to 1$, confirms the normalization.

The two terms cancel to leading order when $\tau\lambda \ll 1$, costing about
$\epsilon/(\tau\lambda)$ in relative accuracy. At the bottom of the parameter
box, $\tau = 10^{-6}$ and $\lambda = 10$, this is still of order $10^{-11}$.
[[numcosmo|nc_cluster_richness_projection_eval_int]] additionally selects the
$\mathrm{erfc}$ argument whose value is the small one, so the difference of
cumulatives never subtracts two saturated values.
